payload.prompt: An insurance claims app lets users submit accident photos and ask what is visible. Which inputs can the app send for image analysis?

options.rationale: A prompt can include a text instruction, such as asking what objects are visible in an image. The instruction tells the model what kind of answer is needed.
The prompt can include one or more attached image inputs. This fits an insurance app that needs to inspect accident photos.
Images can be provided as base64-encoded image data. Base64 converts image bytes into safe text that can be embedded in JSON or URLs.

options.error_type: confuses image inputs with video generation REST endpoints
options.rationale: A video job status endpoint is used when polling an asynchronous video generation job. It is not an input for image analysis.
options.better_fit: A video job status endpoint fits after starting a Sora video render job and checking whether it is complete.

feedback.intrinsic: The claims workflow may focus on checking a video job instead of sending the accident photo and question.
feedback.instructional: For image analysis, send a text instruction plus image inputs such as URLs or base64-encoded image data.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Image analysis requests can combine a text instruction with one or more image inputs, including base64-encoded image data.

payload.prompt: A developer is moving a tested image prompt from the Foundry playground into Python code. Which values must the code have to call the deployed model?

options.rationale: The code needs a Foundry resource key for authentication. This is one of the required values for using a Foundry resource with the OpenAI Python SDK.
The client must point to the Foundry endpoint. The endpoint tells the code where the deployed model is hosted.
The model deployment name is passed as MODEL_NAME in code. It identifies the deployed model the request should use.

options.error_type: confuses image analysis setup with video generation settings
options.rationale: Video duration is a parameter for video generation in the Foundry playground or REST request. It is not needed to call a deployed image analysis model from Python.
options.better_fit: Video duration fits when generating a video and specifying settings such as dimensions and length.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer may add video settings while missing the connection values needed for image analysis code.
feedback.instructional: For Python image analysis, focus on the resource key, endpoint, and model deployment name.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Python image analysis needs the Foundry resource key, endpoint, and model deployment name to call the deployed model.
